citation: Fraass B, Doppke K, Hunt M, Kutcher G, Starkschall G, Stern R, Van Dyke J. American Association of Physicists in Medicine Radiation Therapy Committee Task Group 53: Quality assurance for clinical radiotherapy treatment planning. Med Phys 25(10):1773-1829.
venue_and_status: Medical Physics, published report (AAPM Report 62); English original not accessed, read via JASTRO Japanese translation
problem: How to build a QA programme for radiotherapy treatment-planning systems, including acceptance, commissioning, periodic QA and software version changes
main_result: Ch. 5: periodic tests do not replace commissioning of a new system or acceptance and commissioning of a new software version; Table 5-1 'Variable': software changes, including the operating system, may require checks and/or recommissioning; daily log of hardware/software changes. App. 1 A1.1.4 (vendor): a new release always creates a QA problem; the user decides whether to install it and how much testing precedes clinical release; the vendor must give enough information to choose what to test without recommissioning the whole system. Table A1-2: vendor documentation for version updates (bugs fixed and implications, new features, components that work differently than before, suggested user tests, beta-test results, procedures to convert old patient and machine data, known bugs). A1.2.5 (user): testing and implementing updates is part of the physicist's clinical responsibility; changes to dose, MU, beam, anatomy-modelling or contour/image input functions need detailed testing.
relevance: The medical-physics precedent the reviewer asked for: acceptance/regression testing of each new software version, with an explicit vendor/user split
not_established: Not about AI or longitudinal measurements; prescribes no specific tests; the English wording was not seen (quotes above are translations from Japanese and must be checked against Med Phys 25:1773)
evidence_depth: full_text (JASTRO Japanese translation with English headings; English original blocked)

citation: Vandewinckele L, Claessens M, Dinkla A, Brouwer C, Crijns W, Verellen D, van Elmpt W. Overview of artificial intelligence-based applications in radiotherapy: recommendations for implementation and quality assurance. Radiother Oncol 153:55-66.
venue_and_status: Radiotherapy and Oncology, published (CC BY); read publisher PDF from KU Leuven Lirias
problem: How to commission, implement and quality-assure AI applications in radiotherapy (3rd ESTRO Physics Workshop consensus)
main_result: Fig. 2 caption: 'For major model updates, one should go back to the first phase. For minor updates, only the second phase is repeated.' Implementation: after retraining 'it is important to (re)commission the model with a new validation and test set and repeat the end-to-end test.' Routine model QA: a QMP 'to verify that the model is still valid after a (minor) software update'; 'The reference dataset should be re-predicted on a regular basis and compared to the initial predictions during commissioning (end-to-end performance) to verify consistency of the model.' Commissioning: commercial models need 'a vendor's validation report'; 'the vendor should provide an annual accuracy assessment protocol'. Table 1 lists volume comparison ('systematic under/over segmentation') among commissioning metrics.
relevance: AI-specific QA guidance that ties model updates to recommissioning and to re-predicting a fixed reference set; supports recommendation (2)
not_established: No paired-timepoint or change-measurement test; consistency is checked against the model's own earlier predictions on a reference set, not as a longitudinal comparison; 'major'/'minor' not operationally defined

citation: Hurkmans C, Bibault JE, Brock KK, van Elmpt W, Feng M, Fuller CD, Jereczek-Fossa BA, Korreman S, Landry G, Madesta F, Mayo C, McWilliam A, Moura F, Muren LP, El Naqa I, Seuntjens J, Valentini V, Velec M. venue_and_status: Radiotherapy and Oncology, published (CC BY); read publisher PDF (Aarhus University Pure copy)
problem: Joint European-North American guideline for developing, validating and reporting AI models in radiotherapy
method: Delphi process among 18 authors; 19 statements graded highly recommended/recommended
main_result: Section 'Model QA/updates and upgrades': two procedures are needed in clinical routine, periodic QA because performance 'may drift over time', and 'an update (typically referred to small model changes) or an upgrade (for more substantial changes) procedure'; with periodic retraining 'validation and test procedures of these models need preferably to be fully automated'. Statement 16: 'Have procedures in place for periodic QA of your AI tool before clinical introduction (highly recommended)'. Statement 17: 'Have procedures in place for upgrades and updates before clinical introduction (highly recommended)'. Statement 3: DL reconstruction should be designated 'at the level of the vendor-supplied software version'.
relevance: ESTRO and AAPM jointly endorse an update/upgrade procedure; non-US and medical-physics framing for recommendation (2)
not_established: Does not say what an update validation should measure; no longitudinal or change-measurement criterion; model datasheets (appendices) not read

citation: Brady AP, Allen B, Chong J, Kotter E, Kottler N, Mongan J, Oakden-Rayner L, dos Santos DP, Tang A, Wald C, Slavotinek J. venue_and_status: Insights into Imaging, published (CC BY); simultaneously in Radiol Artif Intell 6:e230513, J Am Coll Radiol, J Med Imaging Radiat Oncol and Can Assoc Radiol J

main_result: Section 7, Periodic monitoring: 'Another specific scenario which may require a re-evaluation of a model's performance would be the issuance of a new model version by the manufacturer. It cannot be simply assumed by user sites that intended benefits introduced by a manufacturer's deployment of the latest version of a model automatically generalize to the local practice.' Section 5: post-market QA plans matter because of concept drift 'or occasionally even differences due to upgrades of successive new versions of AI software'; suggests 'a constant reserved held-out set of test case examples'. Section 7: monitoring by report concordance 'may not work for quantitative outputs'.
relevance: International radiology (diagnostic) societies: a vendor's new model version warrants local re-evaluation; supports recommendations (2) and (3) beyond the USA
not_established: Re-evaluation is framed as performance/generalization, not compatibility with stored measurements; 'may require', not a requirement

citation: Geurts MW, Jacqmin DJ, Jones LE, Kry SF, Mihailidis DN, Ohrt JD, Ritter T, Smilowitz JB, Wingreen NE. AAPM Medical Physics Practice Guideline 5.b: Commissioning and QA of treatment planning dose calculations - megavoltage photon and electron beams. J Appl Clin Med Phys 23(9):e13641.

citation: Huo Z, Summers RM, Paquerault S, Lo J, Hoffmeister J, Armato SG, Freedman MT, Lin J, Lo SCB, Petrick N, Sahiner B, Fryd D, Yoshida H, Chan HP. Quality assurance and training procedures for computer-aided detection and diagnosis systems in clinical use. Med Phys 40(7):077001.
venue_and_status: Medical Physics, published (AAPM Computer Aided Detection Subcommittee); read PMC author manuscript PMC5438240
problem: QA and training procedures for CAD systems at clinical sites
main_result: II.A R1(a): QA test at 'the first installation or subsequent CAD software upgrades, including operating system upgrades'; R4 note 3: 'sensitivity and specificity performance will change with each version of software ... CAD output such as the locations of CAD marks or segmentation boundaries may also change'; R6(b): 'For CAD system upgrades: tolerance limits if performance decreases but no limit on improvement'. II.B.1: 'For an upgrade of the CAD software, the manufacturer should inform the site personnel of any expected changes. The site personnel should be advised to compare the CAD results before and after the upgrade and communicate any unexpected differences.' II.B.3: 'A fixed set of test cases is recommended for acceptance testing at the first installation and subsequent upgrades'. III.B: 'The vendor should provide detailed documentation regarding what has been changed'. V.C: 'Recording the version of the CAD system ... would allow relevant stratified analyses'.
relevance: Diagnostic-imaging analogue to TG-53: before/after comparison on a fixed set at each upgrade, explicit vendor/site split, version recording; notes that segmentation boundaries change with versions
not_established: Pre-deep-learning CAD; tolerance only for performance decreases, so an accuracy-improving but measurement-shifting upgrade would pass; no longitudinal measurement

citation: International Atomic Energy Agency. Commissioning and Quality Assurance of Computerized Planning Systems for Radiation Treatment of Cancer. Technical Reports Series No. 430. Vienna: IAEA.
venue_and_status: IAEA Technical Reports Series No. 430, STI/DOC/010/430, ISBN 92-0-105304-5; official IAEA PDF
problem: International guidance on TPS commissioning and QA
main_result: 10.3.4: 'Vendors usually provide release notes ... If they do not provide these, request such information'; 'If an algorithm is added or altered, differences from previous versions ... should be determined and documented'; 'It is not sufficient to check those elements known to have changed. A standard set of plans should be checked ... Compare plans performed with the new version with the same plans performed with the old version'; 'If no algorithm changes are expected, confirm that the calculation results are identical'; 'it is important to create a transition plan'. 10.3.3: some systems 'invalidate previously stored treatment plans when recalled'; document the changeover date. 7.7.1(e) vendor: 'Detailed information regarding software updates'; 7.7.2(f) user: 'Implementation, commissioning and QA of software upgrades, including detailed documentation'. 6.8: keep 'clear records of which versions of the software have been installed, with dates'.
relevance: International (non-US) statement of version-to-version regression testing and of vendor/user duties; strongest English operative text for the reviewer's TG-53 point
not_established: TPS dose calculation, not segmentation or AI; single-timepoint consistency

citation: Schuring D, Westendorp H, van der Bijl E, Bol G, Crijns W, Delor A, Jourani Y, Loon Ong C, Penninkhof J, Kierkels R, Verbakel W, van de Water T, van de Kamer J. venue_and_status: NCS report (July 2022), open access
problem: Practical verification of TPS installations, updates and upgrades
main_result: 6.1: 'Before a new version of the software can be used safely in the clinic, it needs to be tested to detect any changes in behaviour'; upgrades include 'changes to the underlying algorithms that might change the behaviour and outcomes of the system (e.g. of contours, dose or treatment plans)'; for updates 'the primary goal for testing is to verify the consistency ... in the new version compared to the currently used clinical version'. 6.2: review release notes ('not all changes might be documented'); 'Consider what workflow is needed for patients that are already in the treatment preparation phase during the clinical release'; 'Document the exact (sub)version of the new installation, as well as the date at which it was introduced'; prepare a roll-back. Table 6.1 item 3: 'Import structures from the previous version and check for consistency in contour representation and volume calculation.'
relevance: European regression-testing guideline that already checks volume consistency across versions and flags patients in progress during a version change
not_established: TPS volume calculation of the same contour, not re-segmentation by a changed model; no longitudinal change error

citation: International Atomic Energy Agency. Clinical Implementation of Artificial Intelligence Systems in Medical Imaging and Radiotherapy: Guidelines for Medical Physicists. IAEA Human Health Series No. 50. Vienna: IAEA.
venue_and_status: IAEA Human Health Series No. 50 (May 2026), STI/PUB/2135, ISBN 978-92-0-130026-3; read from a third-party copy with matching colophon
problem: Lifecycle guidance for clinically qualified medical physicists implementing imaging-based AI in imaging and radiotherapy
main_result: 5.4.6.1: 'the CQMP and their team need to verify the performance level of the AI system before and after updates or upgrades ... using, for example, reference data composed of both manufacturer and organization test sets', and define update requirements including a manufacturer testing environment and 'rollback to previous versions'. 5.4.6.2: the agreement 'has to define a clear separation between the responsibilities of the manufacturer and the responsibilities of the healthcare organization'. 5.6: 'In the event of system or model updates or upgrades, the CQMP will lead a new round of acceptance and commissioning'. 5.6.10: the CQMP 'may need to conduct acceptance testing again'. 5.8.3: ad hoc QC after 'the release of a new version of the AI system'; 'If ad hoc QC testing fails during commissioning of a new version ... the new version cannot be released for clinical use.' Table 2 lists Dice and Hausdorff distance as common metrics for tumour segmentation used for 'Follow-up or response monitoring (e.g. RECIST)'.
relevance: Most recent and most specific medical-physics guidance on AI updates (international); its Table 2 shows that overlap metrics are the default even for follow-up use, which the paper's result qualifies
not_established: No paired-timepoint or between-version measurement test; authors should check quotes against the official IAEA PDF

main_result: Section 6: 'a retrained model should be labelled with a new version number and undergo a proportionate evaluation prior to clinical use, as would be performed for an updated radiotherapy treatment planning system'; models 'are not fully deterministic', so a change of hardware, library or memory 'may result in different performance of the same model'; DICOM can encode 'software systems and versions', but when data move between systems 'the output ... may reconstruct a new DICOM image without preserving all previous information', 'breaking the audit trail'; store the original DICOM objects; re-evaluate against a local test library 'at least once a year and with any change in imaging system'.

citation: Barati R, Duan J, Gao S, Zhao Y, Chen X, Yu C, Xu Z, Khaleghibizaki M, Lofman F, Ohrt J, Court L, Balter P, Yang J. Clinical evaluation and regression test of a commercial deep-learning auto-segmentation model. J Appl Clin Med Phys 27(10):e70824.

problem: Regression testing of a vendor DL auto-segmentation model after a software upgrade

citation: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, Health Canada, Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency. Predetermined Change Control Plans for Machine Learning-Enabled Medical Devices: Guiding Principles.
venue_and_status: Joint guiding principles (October 2023; GOV.UK first published 24 October 2023); official FDA page, PDF and GOV.UK page
problem: Characteristics of robust PCCPs for ML-enabled devices
method: Joint regulator principles (FDA, Health Canada, MHRA)
main_result: Defines a PCCP as 'a plan, proposed by a manufacturer, that specifies: certain planned modifications to a device; the protocol for implementing and controlling those modifications and the assessment of impacts from modifications'. Principle 1: methods 'for verifying and validating the changes and mechanisms to detect and revert or stop implementation of a change that fails to meet specified performance criteria'. Principle 3: methods that 'demonstrate the benefits and risks of the device before and after changes'. Principle 4 (Transparent): 'detailed plans for ongoing transparency to users', including 'characterization of the device before and after implementation of changes'.
relevance: Makes the paper's PCCP sentence non-US-only; supports reporting before/after characterization

citation: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 June 2024 laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence (Artificial Intelligence Act). OJ L, 2024/1689, 12.7.2024.
venue_and_status: EU regulation in force (original OJ text; amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)
problem: Horizontal EU rules for AI systems, including high-risk AI in medical devices
main_result: Art. 3(23): 'substantial modification' means 'a change to an AI system after its placing on the market or putting into service which is not foreseen or planned in the initial conformity assessment carried out by the provider and as a result of which the compliance ... is affected or results in a modification to the intended purpose'. Art. 43(4): such systems 'shall undergo a new conformity assessment procedure in the event of a substantial modification, regardless of whether the modified system is intended to be further distributed or continues to be used by the current deployer'; 'For high-risk AI systems that continue to learn ..., changes ... that have been pre-determined by the provider at the moment of the initial conformity assessment and are part of the information contained in the technical documentation referred to in point 2(f) of Annex IV, shall not constitute a substantial modification.' Art. 25(1)(b): a deployer that makes a substantial modification becomes the provider. Art. 26(1),(5),(6): deployers use systems per instructions, 'monitor the operation', keep logs at least six months. Art. 13(3)(c),(e): instructions for use state pre-determined changes and maintenance 'including as regards software updates'. Annex IV 1(a): technical documentation gives 'the version of the system reflecting its relation to previous versions'; 1(c): 'requirements related to version updates'. Recital 128: changes that may affect compliance (e.g. 'change of operating system or software architecture') make it a new system.
relevance: Requested EU provisions with exact article numbers; frames updates, version identification and deployer duties
not_established: The pre-determined-change exemption is worded for systems that 'continue to learn'; Commission guidelines on substantial modification (Art. 96(1)(c)) not found; no measurement-compatibility provision

citation: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 8 July 2026 amending Regulations (EU) 2024/1689, (EU) 2018/1139 and (EU) 2023/1230 as regards the simplification of the implementation of harmonised rules on artificial intelligence (Digital Omnibus on AI). OJ L, 2026/1744, 24.7.2026.
venue_and_status: EU regulation in force (third day after publication)
problem: Simplification and postponement of AI Act obligations
main_result: Amended Art. 113: Chapter III Sections 1-3 apply from '2 December 2027 as regards AI systems classified as high-risk pursuant to Article 6(2) and Annex III' and '2 August 2028 as regards AI systems classified as high-risk pursuant to Article 6(1) and Annex I'. Art. 111(2) now refers to systems placed on the market before the Chapter III application date and to 'significant changes in their designs'. Art. 43(3) replaced; Art. 3(23) and 43(4) unchanged.
relevance: Needed if the revision states when AI Act obligations apply to AI medical devices (no longer 2 August 2027)
not_established: Does not change the substantial-modification concept

citation: Regulation (EU) 2017/745 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 5 April 2017 on medical devices. OJ L 117, 5.5.2017, p. 1-175.
venue_and_status: EU regulation in force (original OJ text read; later amendments not checked for these provisions)
problem: EU medical-device rules, including change control and device identification
main_result: Annex IX Ch. II 4.10: 'Changes to the approved device shall require approval from the notified body ... where such changes could affect the safety and performance of the device or the conditions prescribed for use' (Section 4 covers class III and certain class IIb devices). Annex IX 2.4: manufacturer informs the notified body of 'any plan for substantial changes' to the QMS or device range. Annex VI Part C 6.5.2: 'A new UDI-DI shall be required whenever there is a modification that changes: (a) the original performance; (b) the safety or the intended use of the software; (c) interpretation of data', including 'new or modified algorithms'; 6.5.3: minor revisions get a new UDI-PI; 6.5.4(b): UDI shown on an easily accessible screen.

not_established: Whether a given retraining changes 'performance' enough for a new UDI-DI is a manufacturer/notified-body judgement; Section 4.10 scope is limited

citation: Dayma K, Patel P, Hildreth K, Jamaspishvili T. Predetermined Change Control Plan Adoption and Documentation Transparency in U.S. Food and Drug Administration-cleared Radiology Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning Devices. Radiol Artif Intell 8(5):e260385.

problem: How radiology AI devices use PCCPs and how transparently
method: Cross-sectional scoping review of FDA databases through April 2026; 8-point documentation rubric
